subject: URGENT: ParcelPro production spike — request immediate config rollback
messages:
From: ParcelPro SRE <sre@parcelpro.com>
To: aditya.rao@redwood.com
Cc: sam.torres@parcelpro.com
Date: Mon, 21 May 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production degradation: high latency and 5xx surge

Aditya —

We started seeing a sustained latency increase at 08:45 PT and a correlated jump in 5xx responses for text-generate routes. Error rate went from ~0.2% to ~5% and p95 doubled. Our team traced it to heavy queueing on a subset of routes hitting your LLM pool.

We attached a short extract of service logs and a snapshot of your KV config. It looks like aggressive prefix-matching and a recent policy change that expanded cached prefixes for ParcelPro. Now dozens of short-lived keys are thrashing the cache and causing head-of-line queues on GPU lanes.

We need an immediate rollback of the config that was applied at 08:12 PT and a temporary rate-limiter or queue cap while you investigate — otherwise this impacts our customer SLAs today. Can you confirm next steps and ETA?

Thanks,
— ParcelPro SRE (Sam)

Attachments: service-logs-2028-05-21.tar.gz, kv_policy_snapshot.json
From: aditya.rao@redwood.com

ETA: rollback + temporary cap in ~18 minutes. I’ll confirm when done and share the play-by-play.

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll treat this as a P1.

- enable short-term queue trimming for lanes showing >120ms queue time

Laura — status and quick ask:

Thanks for the rollback. Initial metrics look better for ParcelPro p95 at the edge, but we’re still seeing tail latency jitter on small-sequence requests. Early signal suggests the following combined factors:

- recent batching policy change (auto-agg window set to 30ms for low-latency lanes) increased splice opportunities but also led to batch starvation when KV cache misses spike
- aggressive prefix caching expanded the working set which increased KV miss penalties and led to HOL (head-of-line) stalls on the batching queues.

Immediate recommendation: disable the 30ms auto-agg for ParcelPro for the next 6 hours and force single-request fast-path for sequences <64 tokens. That will trade a bit of throughput for predictable latency while we tune cache sizing and prefix eviction heuristics.

Can Marissa and Stephanie run a targeted simulation on the 08:00–09:30 traffic slice to verify impact? If confirmed, we can push the temporary policy change and then schedule a controlled rollout of a corrected prefix-eviction policy.

— Rishi
Head of Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Production degradation: high latency and 5xx surge — post-update summary

Team / Sam —

Quick status update and next steps after the emergency window:

What we did (timeline):
- 08:12: prefix-expansion policy deployed (automated rollout) — introduced large number of short-lived keys
- 08:45: ParcelPro reports spike in latency/5xxs (queueing observed)
- 09:33: rollback initiated by Redwood (Laura) — immediate reduction in queueing
- 10:00: applied emergency per-route concurrency cap and token-bucket burst control
- 10:12: disabled 30ms auto-agg for ParcelPro and enabled single-request fast-path for <64 tokens

Impact observed:
- p95 for ParcelPro dropped from ~780ms to ~210ms within 12 minutes of rollback
- 5xx rate returned to baseline (~0.3%) after caps and fast-path enabled
- overall cluster throughput dropped ~6% for a 6-hour stabilization window (expected and acceptable trade-off)

Action items (owners & timing):
- Rishi + Marissa: 72-hour simulation run with the 08:00–09:30 traffic slice and proposed eviction-policy patch (start now, deliver by 2028-05-25)
- Stephanie: prepare a safelist / prefix-whitelist approach for high-cardinality customers to avoid global prefix-expansion (deliverable 2028-05-24)
- Laura: follow up with ParcelPro SRE on the residual logs and share a short incident timeline (today)
- Aditya: schedule a leadership sync if there’s a customer exec ask (I’m available 16:00 PT)

Sam — we’re going to keep a dedicated monitor on your routes for 48 hours and will provide a runbook for you to throttle or move traffic to dedicated capacity if you prefer. I’ll also send a short post-mortem when we have the simulation results.

Appreciate your patience — we’ll own this and make the config path safer.

— Aditya Rao
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
